desc.p: Creates a user account, as the site's own registration form does, and sends the site's activation mail. The account can't be used until it is activated with the code from that mail (services/users/activate). Like on the website, an account that is never activated is deleted after 14 days.

Only for applications the site's administrators allowed to register users, and only over HTTPS (the request carries a password). Check has_registration in services/apisrv/installation first; it also gives the URLs of the pages the user accepts.

The checks are the website's. A refused value gives HTTP 400 with the parameter's name in parameter and a fixed code in reason, so the application can show it at the right field: username_invalid, username_taken, email_invalid, email_taken, password_invalid, password_weak. The readable text is in whats_wrong_about_it.

req.name: username
req.p: 3 to 60 letters, digits or . - _ @ = ( ) / \ & * + ~ #; spaces only inside the name; not an email address; not taken.

req.name: email
req.p: The user's email address (at most 60 characters); the activation mail goes there. It must not belong to another account.

req.name: password
req.p: 6 to 60 letters, digits, spaces or . - _ @ = ( ) / \ & * + ~ #, at least 5 different characters, not containing the username, "open", "cache" or "caching", and not one of the site's list of common passwords.

req.name: accept_terms
req.p: true: the user has read and accepted the terms of service, the privacy statement and the data license (terms_url, privacy_url and data_license_url in services/apisrv/installation). Show them with links before the user confirms.

opt.name: langpref
opt.p: Language of the activation mail: German for de, English otherwise. Default: the site's language.

returns.p: A dictionary with the account's username and email as stored.
